page: Microsoft Azure E2pds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an ARM64 Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processor. It features 2 dedicated physical cores running at 3.0 GHz with a 1:1 thread-to-core ratio, meaning hyperthreading is disabled. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It includes 77 GB of local storage and supports Premium Storage.

Benchmark data indicates moderate single-core performance but limited multi-core scaling. The stress-ng single-core CPU test scores in the average range at 1791.39, and single-threaded gzip compression reaches 23.89 GB/sec. However, multi-core benchmarks, such as Geekbench at 1978.0 and stress-ng multi-core at 3552.48, fall into the lower performance tiers. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with uncached read speeds at 27.08 GB/sec and write speeds at 16.68 GB/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers a high memory density per vCPU on an ARM architecture, which typically translates to lower operational costs compared to x86 equivalents. However, users face performance tradeoffs, particularly in compute-heavy workloads, cryptographic operations, and LLM inference, where the lack of advanced vector extensions and lower multi-threaded performance are apparent.

The E2pds_v5 is suited for memory-intensive but compute-light workloads. Appropriate use cases include small-scale caching layers, lightweight database hosting, Redis key-value stores, and basic web serving where memory capacity is prioritized over raw processing power.
